script: "Friends vanished overnight—now my texts feel like echoes from a dead world.". I was born in the '80s, so I grew up with dial‑up and mixtapes, not TikTok. Back in the day, my phone was a constant ring, my friends were my squad, and we'd text at 3 a.male. about everything—Laughing out loud, literally. Fast forward to 2024, and my squad's basically ghost town. I hit up a guy from college, and his reply comes after a month. I text my mom‑friend, and she's like, "I am swamped, sorry." (I know, right?) My vibe? I am a social butterfly, not a hermit. But now, the only people I get real convo from are like, 2 or 3. The rest? Silent. It feels like I am living in a bubble with no one to pop it. I am in my late 40s, no kids, no "Mom squad," and my husband is the only person who actually gets me. I volunteer at a nonprofit that's totally my jam—just one person from there, but I am good at that. I work for the city, which is solid, but there's no room for friendship at work. It's all politics, no play. So, what's the deal? The "everyone's too busy" line is literally insane. My parents had a whole circle of friends, so how does anyone even say that? The stakes? I am losing the human connection that kept me sane. I used to roll to the skating rink, hit the bowling alley, dance at high school parties. Those were my lifelines. Now, the silence is louder than any music. I can't even text someone and get a "I'll get back to you later" within a week. It's like I am stuck in a time warp where everyone else is moving on, and I am the only one still waiting. I am not looking for a rescue mission; I just want to feel seen again. If this didn't feel like a loss, then I'd be the one with the biggest ego. I've tried reaching out—texts, calls, even a "hey, want to grab coffee?"—and the responses are either "I am swamped" or a one‑word "ok." It's like the social fabric ripped right in the middle of my life. The only thing I have is my husband, who's amazing, but I need more than that. I need friends who remember what it's like to laugh until your stomach hurts, who can share a meme or a story without pretending. The irony? I am the one who used to be the life of the party, now I am the one who's left on the sidelines. I feel like a ghost in my own social scene. The world's moved on, but I am still here, holding onto the echo of my own laughter. I am not looking for a grand finale; I just want the next chapter to have a few more characters. If anyone else is feeling the same, let's not stay silent. Let's start talking again.
